conditions: The applicability is a signature file and its corresponding implementation during the compilation described in §§11 and 12.1–12.2.
limitations: The captured F# 4.1 working document records May 2018 updates, omits some F# 4.1 RFCs, and warns of implementation discrepancies. Other RFCs, releases, and compiler behavior require separate evidence.
This is the documented file-signature boundary. It does not assert a particular reflection or ABI result, that runtime code is removed, or that scripts can have a corresponding signature file.

triggers: A changed publisher representation, applicable omitted RFC, source correction or contrary scoped evidence.

statement: The F# 4.1 working specification checks an implementation file’s inferred signature against any required signature. Its resulting signature is the required one when present and the inferred signature otherwise. A corresponding signature file can hide functionality present in the implementation file.
